sentences.text: Microtuban is known only from a single partially preserved skeleton that lacks the skull, designated as holotype SMNK PAL 6595.
The fossil's upper arm measured about nine centimeters and the lower arm about seven centimeters.
The fourth metacarpal of the specimen is 122 millimeters long.
Microtuban possesses two unique traits: the second wing-finger phalanx is long at 85% of the first phalanx's length, and the fourth phalanx is extremely reduced at 1.1% of the wing-finger length.
Possible juvenile traits in the specimen include the lack of a notarium and unfused scapula and coracoid bones.
The articulated but broken bones suggest it died from a collision or a predator bite before sinking to the sea bottom.
The holotype was collected in the early Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 99.6 to 96 million years ago, from the Sannine Formation in Lebanon.
Microtuban was named by Ross A. Elgin and Eberhard Frey in 2011, with the type species Microtuban altivolans.
The species name derives from the Latin words for 'high' and 'to fly'.
Microtuban was assigned to the Azhdarchoidea superfamily using the comparative method.
A 2018 study by Nicholas Longrich and colleagues placed Microtuban within the Chaoyangopteridae at the basalmost position.
It is impossible to definitively classify Microtuban as a thalassodromid or chaoyangopterid because the distinguishing traits are located in the skull, which is missing from the holotype.
Microtuban lived during the Cenomanian stage, from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
